text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 5

Both you and the appointed candidate are women, so the panel's composition can't explain the outcome in terms of sex — there's no asymmetry to point to. Raising it would likely read as grasping, and could undermine the credible part of your case.

The real issue is substantive: you appear to hold stronger formal qualifications (PhD vs. master's) and eight years of section leadership, yet "broad leadership experience" and a management course were decisive. That's worth probing — the panel may have weighted operational/managerial breadth, budget responsibility or staff-relations experience over scientific depth, which is a legitimate but arguable choice.

Send a written follow-up requesting the explanation you're entitled to, citing your original date. Ask specifically how criteria were weighted.
